27 An electromagnetic wave travelling in free space is not visible to the human eye.
What is a possible wavelength of the wave?
A
4.5  10–10
km
B
6.2  10–7
m
C
5.4  10–6
cm
D
4.2  10–4
mm

hints: Recall the visible range in metres is roughly $4.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, so a non-visible wave must convert to well outside this interval.
Convert each mixed unit to metres using $1 \text{ km} = 10^3 \text{ m}$, $1 \text{ cm} = 10^{-2} \text{ m}$ and $1 \text{ mm} = 10^{-3} \text{ m}$ before comparing.
Check which converted value is an order of magnitude smaller than $10^{-7} \text{ m}$ and therefore lies in the ultraviolet region rather than visible light.
walkthrough: Visible light in free space has wavelength from about $400 \text{ nm}$ to $700 \text{ nm}$, i.e. $4.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Convert all options to metres to allow direct comparison with the visible range.
Option A: $4.5 \times 10^{-10} \text{ km} \times 10^3 = 4.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$. Option B is already $6.2 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Option C: $5.4 \times 10^{-6} \text{ cm} \times 10^{-2} = 5.4 \times 10^{-8} \text{ m}$. Option D: $4.2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mm} \times 10^{-3} = 4.2 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.

Values of $4.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, $6.2 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ and $4.2 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ all lie between $4.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ and $7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, so they are visible.
$5.4 \times 10^{-8} \text{ m}$ is about ten times shorter than violet light and lies in the ultraviolet part of the electromagnetic spectrum, so it is not visible. This is option C.

A.explanation: $4.5 \times 10^{-10} \text{ km} = 4.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, about $450 \text{ nm}$, which lies inside the visible range of about $400$ to $700 \text{ nm}$.

B.explanation: $6.2 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, about $620 \text{ nm}$, is red light and is clearly visible to the human eye.

C.explanation: $5.4 \times 10^{-6} \text{ cm} = 5.4 \times 10^{-8} \text{ m}$, about $54 \text{ nm}$, which is ultraviolet and shorter than visible light.

D.explanation: $4.2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mm} = 4.2 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, about $420 \text{ nm}$, which lies inside the visible violet region.
